svg.title: Agulhas source-tagged pathway fate sensitivity
svg.desc: One hundred eight deterministic upstream pathway trials produce fourteen Cape Basin crossings, twenty-four return-corridor crossings, sixty-two unresolved paths, and eight terminations under the baseline gates. Nearby gate definitions change the census.
svg.metadata: Natural Earth SHA-256 9e0729ee253ca7d7a5c4ae9395fb1902264c5377c52e224d13dd85010e2835d9. The ensemble tests release-position, release-time, and fate-gate sensitivity in one historical nominal-15-m OSCAR year. Counts are method outcomes, not leakage percentages, probabilities, volume or heat transports, water-mass identities, eddy tracking, climatology, or overturning estimates. Unresolved means neither declared threshold was reached within 150 days.
svg.text: THE FATE DEPENDS ON WHERE YOU DRAW THE GATE.
Four upstream centers × nine nearby seeds × three release dates · 150 days · deterministic surface pathways

g.text: Most paths reach neither threshold within 150 days.
That unresolved majority is part of the result.
NO TRACK IS A UNIT OF WATER, VOLUME, OR HEAT.

svg.text: NINE REASONABLE GATE PAIRS · NINE DIFFERENT CENSUSES
C = Cape Basin · R = return corridor · U = unresolved · T = terminated. Gold outline marks the baseline.

g.text: Gate placement is a method choice,

svg.text: NOMINAL 15 M · ONE HISTORICAL OSCAR YEAR · EQUAL-COUNT METHOD ENSEMBLE · STRICT WET STENCIL · NO DIFFUSION · NOT PROBABILITY, VOLUME, HEAT, OR CLIMATOLOGY
